jess (support): FYI escalation from @raj — customer hitting tool/function-call failures when using our OpenAI-compatible spec. They say the assistant picks the right tool name but args fail schema validation (enum/casing mismatch). Request ID: req_0xabc123. Repro + logs below.

raj (customer): repro minimal:
```json
POST /v1/chat/completions
{
  \"model\": \"gpt-4o-mini\",
  \"messages\": [{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"parse invoice\"}],
  \"functions\": [
    {\"name\": \"extract\", \"parameters\": {\"type\": {\"type\": \"string\", \"enum\": [\"INVOICE\", \"RECEIPT\"]}, \"url\": {\"type\": \"string\"}}}
  ],
  \"function_call\": \"auto\"
}
```

Response we see (tool chosen but args invalid):
```json
{
  \"id\": \"resp_123\",
  \"choices\": [
    {
      \"message\": {
        \"role\": \"tool\",
        \"name\": \"extract\",
        \"content\": \"{\\\"type\\\":\\\"invoice\\\",\\\"url\\\":\\\"https://...\\\"}\"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

support-bot: req_0xabc123 -> backend error 400 schema_error enum mismatch: expected one of [INVOICE, RECEIPT] got 'invoice' (lowercase).

sam (eng): Are they on Hosted API or Dedicated? Does the customer have any compat flags enabled?

raj (customer): Hosted API, no special flags. Happens for many invoices. We only see lowercase enum from the model side, which then fails validation in our function-calling layer.

maria (ml): This looks like two incompat issues hitting together: (1) enum casing/aliasing (models returning lowercase or synonyms) and (2) field name aliasing — some users/tool implementations send `doc_type` instead of `type`. We need a tolerant deserializer.

sam (eng): Quick plan: add an \"openai-compat normalizer\" step before JSON schema validation that a) normalizes enum casing/aliases, b) maps known field aliases, and c) logs original vs normalized payload for audit. Can we accept lowercase synonyms for the enum? E.g. map {invoice, Invoice, INVOICE} -> INVOICE.

jess (support): Customer asked for ETA, their integration is blocked.

sam (eng): I'll push a small hotfix in the hosted request pipeline to run normalization pre-validation. Patch will: 1) case-insensitive enum match, 2) alias mapping table (doc_type -> type), 3) permissive JSON parsing for stringified function args. Example normalizer rules:
```js
const enumMap = { invoice: 'INVOICE', receipt: 'RECEIPT' }
function normalizeArgs(raw) {
  const parsed = typeof raw === 'string' ? JSON.parse(raw) : raw
  const normalized = {}
  normalized.type = enumMap[(parsed.type || parsed.doc_type || '').toLowerCase()] || parsed.type
  normalized.url = parsed.url || parsed.link
  return normalized
}
```

maria (ml): Also log a short hash of the original model output to help debug model-side aliasing. We should make the mapping configurable per-customer.

sam (eng): Deploy plan: canary to 2% hosted traffic -> monitor schema-error-rate and function-failures for 30m -> roll to 100% if no regressions. Then coordinate with Dedicated images for a minor release.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for openai-compat-normalizer (release r2024-06-18-hotfix) — 2% traffic.

jess (support): Pushed repro to the canary logs, customer confirmed they can reproduce against canary. Can you add a temporary header we can use to force normalization for their requests while we roll?

sam (eng): Yep — header `X-Compat-Normalize: true` accepted. I'll enable it for the customer's API key ID (acct_raj_77) after rollout.

deploy-bot: Canary metrics after 15m: schema_error rate down 92% for requests with normalization. No increased latency observed.

raj (customer): confirmed on our side — function now executes and parsing succeeds. Thanks! :tada:

jess (support): Marking resolved for now. Followups: add integration test for case-insensitive enums and add docs note about common aliases.

sam (eng): Filing PR for the normalizer + tests, will backport to Dedicated. Assigning to @sam.

maria (ml): We should also add a short eval to our model onboarding to catch enum aliasing patterns in candidate models.

jess (support): Closing thread once PR is merged and Dedicated patch scheduled. :white_check_mark:
